transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I've been struggling a lot lately because I feel like I just can't listen when people are talking directly to me. I'm constantly getting distracted by my own thoughts and feel too restless to just sit still. It's starting to really impact my daily life, so I wanted to get some help.
When you feel restless, do you find it difficult to control your impulses, such as interrupting others during conversations or acting before thinking?
I don't really find myself interrupting others or acting without thinking. My restlessness is much more physical, like I constantly need to fidget with my hands or tap my feet.

Do you often find that you lose or misplace essential items like your keys, phone, or wallet, or do you frequently make careless mistakes in your work or daily tasks because you aren't paying close enough attention to details?
No, I don't really lose my things or make careless mistakes very often. I'm actually pretty good at keeping track of my keys and phone.
Have you experienced these symptoms of inattention and restlessness since you were a child, or did they only begin to develop later in your life?
Yes, I've actually had these struggles since I was a child. I distinctly remember having trouble paying attention and constantly fidgeting back in elementary school, definitely before I turned 12.

When you are in situations where you are required to remain seated, such as in a classroom or during meetings, do you find it extremely difficult to stay still, often feeling a strong internal need to get up or move around?

Yes, definitely. I find it really hard to stay seated during long meetings or lectures, and I constantly feel this strong urge to get up and walk around or stretch. Even when I know I'm expected to stay in my seat, I often end up finding an excuse to stand up.
Do you often find yourself talking excessively, or do you frequently feel as though you are 'on the go' or driven by an internal motor?
No, I don't really feel like I'm constantly "on the go" or driven by a motor like that. I also don't think I talk excessively, as I'm usually on the quieter side during conversations.
